title: Doubling Revenue at a DTC Skincare Brand
prompt: Your client is a direct-to-consumer (DTC) skincare brand that wants to double revenue in three years. They sell online, are profitable, and have loyal repeat customers. How should they do it?
background: They sell through their own website and Amazon; no physical retail.

clarifying_answers.What is the goal: Double revenue from $50M to $100M within three years.
clarifying_answers.What channels: DTC website plus Amazon today; open to new channels.
clarifying_answers.Profitability constraint: Growth should keep the business profitable, not buy revenue at a loss.
clarifying_answers.Any product constraints: Open to new products, bundles, and subscription.

exhibits.name: Revenue Build
exhibits.data: Revenue = customers x orders per year x average order value (AOV). Today: 500,000 customers x 2 orders/year x $50 AOV = $50M.

exhibits.name: Unit Economics
exhibits.data: New-customer acquisition cost (CAC) is $40; customer lifetime value (LTV) is $150; annual retention is 60%. Retail/wholesale could expand reach beyond the current base.

good_framework: Decompose revenue = customers x frequency x AOV; each is a growth lever.
Customers: paid acquisition (is LTV:CAC healthy enough to spend more?), new channels (retail/wholesale).
Keep it profitable; prioritize the highest-leverage lever given loyal repeat behavior.

quant.question: Find one combination of levers that roughly doubles revenue to ~$100M.
quant.work: 700,000 customers x 2.5 orders/year x $55 AOV ≈ $96.25M — close to the $100M target.

quant.question: Is the acquisition engine healthy enough to spend more on growth?
quant.work: $150 LTV / $40 CAC = 3.75:1, comfortably above the ~3:1 rule of thumb, so there's room to invest in acquisition.

recommendation: Pull all three levers, led by subscription. A healthy LTV:CAC of 3.75:1 means they can profitably acquire more customers; raising AOV (bundles/premium) and frequency (a replenishment subscription, which fits their loyal repeat base) does the rest — e.g., 700k customers x 2.5 orders x $55 ≈ $96M. Add retail/wholesale for reach. Subscription is the highest-leverage move because it lifts both frequency and retention at once.
